cells.tense: You're in the middle of it, and the seeing comes clear because you kept showing up — today, with your hands in the work and your attention steady.
cells.ask: Let this clear sight go outward without spending it: show one piece of it to one person once, then stop. It turns the light outward without using it up.
cells.core:
This is what it looks like when the practice is going well. You are alone with the work, and the repetition has stopped being effort and become the way you see. Your hands know what to do next, and your eyes have stopped arguing with them. The clarity is not dramatic. It is just steady enough to trust.

So let it out beyond your own room. You do not have to prove it or perfect it — show one piece of what you now see to one person and leave it there. The seeing belongs to you either way; the showing is what makes it visible.
cells.sheetLine: You practice steadily, and because you do, the seeing is clear and available — and you know it is yours.
cells.verb: seeing what is actually there for the first time, before there is anything yet to say about it
cells.place: the quiet room where you practice alone, hour after hour, building skill by repetition

lint.detail: the ask carries no word of the place — the same ask would serve any seat

cells.tense: You're already bracing at a future point, still rehearsing a clarity you don't yet have.
cells.ask: Set the future down for one hour and pick up the simplest unfinished step in front of you — not the completed version. Presence arrives on its own from there.
cells.core:
In a life of steady practice, this capacity would feel like conviction building quietly. But right now you are pushing ahead of the work itself — trying to see the landing before you have taken the next step. You scrutinize every signal for what it might mean later, and the scrutiny has stopped serving the craft. The next clear thing cannot arrive while you keep reaching past it.

So step back into what is actually here. Put down the image of the done version and touch the simplest piece of the practice that is still unfinished. Doing that one ordinary thing returns you to a moment that is fresh and open, and the fresh start can come from where you actually are.
cells.sheetLine: You're trying to see the end before you've done the next step — and it's costing you contact with the work.
cells.verb: seeing what is actually there for the first time, before there is anything yet to say about it
cells.place: the quiet room where you practice alone, hour after hour, building skill by repetition

lint.detail: the ask carries no word of the place — the same ask would serve any seat

cells.tense: You stopped, and you're still standing where you stopped — the practice did not continue, and the clarity did not come back.
cells.ask: Choose one ordinary step of the work you already know how to do and finish it today, then stop. That completion gives back the next direction, earned rather than planned.
cells.core:
When the practice is alive, a small steady light is kept lit by attention rather than flash. Lately that light has gone quiet — not because you lost interest, but because the doing stopped. You know how to practice. You are not doing it. So the seeing has gone flat and ordinary things look blurry, because you have been telling yourself the next step will show up on its own.

It will not. Pick the smallest finished piece you can do today and complete it, and let that one completion be the only direction you need. Finishing it feeds the part of you that knows how to keep going, and the vision comes back through the work itself, not before it.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped the practice, and the seeing has gone flat with it.
cells.verb: seeing what is actually there for the first time, before there is anything yet to say about it
cells.place: the quiet room where you practice alone, hour after hour, building skill by repetition

lint.detail: the ask carries no word of the place — the same ask would serve any seat

cells.tense: You are already seeing clearly — it's happening in the room right now — and you keep describing it as if the work were teaching you instead of you working it.
cells.ask: Say 'this is mine' about one thing you already see because of your practice. That claim returns you to the ground you were already standing on.
cells.core:
You are in a life of steady practice, and the clear seeing you get from it shows up in what you notice without trying. It shapes your choices. It shows in your hands. But the running of it gets attributed to the craft, or to something that just happens to you. Your claim runs ahead of your mouth.

So claim the smallest piece of it. Say to yourself that this one thing is yours — you earned it through repetition — and you will be back at the beginning of clear seeing, which is where the light was all along. It shines because it is, and now you can stand on it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already seeing clearly from the practice; you just haven't called it yours.
cells.verb: seeing what is actually there for the first time, before there is anything yet to say about it
